posts.content:
Great piece in The Robot Report on how we're attacking one of the hardest problems in robotics: manipulation.

Our AMRs have powered 8 billion+ picks. Now we're bringing that same standard to picking itself, with Locus Array and NeuraGrasp, the soft-gripping technology we gained through our Nexera Robotics acquisition.

Roy Belak and his team nailed the philosophy. Reliability first. Quality picks first. Speed comes after. The industry loves to advertise picks per hour. Nobody talks about mispicks, double picks, and product damage. Those are what eat into customer costs.

Suction gets you 60-70% of the way. NeuraGrasp bridges the rest by combining suction and pinch grasping to handle items that used to stop robots cold: porous polybags, cloth, and small containers.

Manipulation isn't a feature for us. It's a pillar of innovation we intend to be exceptional at.

Read the full article: https://lnkd.in/gqERRDwf

#Robotics #WarehouseAutomation #PhysicalAI

When I saw the latest data on warehouse robot orders from A3 - Association for Advancing Automation and Interact Analysis, I was surprised. Companies are juggling new tariffs and higher fuel costs - why are they buying automation?

I talked to the experts and it turns out I had it backward. Businesses are adding more robotics to their warehouses in part *because* of the higher costs. Warehouse wages are way up, and consumers want faster home delivery, making the math easier to get a return on investment with automation.

Another important factor at play: Companies want to add resilience to their supply chains. “Uncertainty really is the thing right now that’s driving a lot of automation purchases,” said Rick Faulk of Locus Robotics.

Thanks to Patrick Kelleher of GXO Logistics, Inc., Rueben Scriven, Jeff Burnstein and everyone else who shared their expertise for this one.

Read more here: https://lnkd.in/gVfcmHwW

“What we planned was actually no longer 100% true.” 

That’s a familiar reality in fulfillment operations. 

What looks right in the planning phase does not always match what operations need once volumes, product categories, and customer requirements become real. 

For MSK Pharma Group, the value was in being able to adjust workflows without starting a long redesign or conversion project.  

So, when the original setup no longer matched MSK’s operational reality, with Locus, the team could remap workflows and introduce changes quickly. 

That included: 
• Adjusting workflows after go-live 

• Remapping processes without long redesign cycles  

• Introducing new product categories into the operation 

• Keeping the site setup flexible as requirements changed  

In this clip, the MSK team explains how flexibility goes beyond day-to-day operations, helping the business manage long-term growth.

Pharmaceutical fulfillment doesn’t leave much room for operational friction. 

Serialization. Lot validation. Expiry-date tracking. High order volumes.  

As demand grew, German Pharmaceutical leader MSK Pharma Group needed fulfillment infrastructure that could scale across both existing and newly developed facilities, without locking operations into rigid automation constraints. 

With Locus Robotics, MSK now operates: 

• 63 robots across two neighboring warehouse sites 
• 55,000+ daily units processed 
• 6,400+ daily order lines handled 

When demand shifts between facilities, robot capacity can be reassigned in approximately 15 minutes. 

In this new video case study, MSK shares how adaptive fulfillment infrastructure helped reduce walking time, improve pick productivity, and support future growth across its pharmaceutical operations.
